problem: LLMs aligned for safety over-refuse benign requests by misclassifying them as toxic, undermining helpfulness without reliably rejecting harmful content.
approach: Introduce DCR (Discernment via Contrastive Refinement), a preceding alignment stage using contrastive learning to help LLMs distinguish truly toxic prompts from superficially toxic ones.
contribution: Reduces over-refusal while preserving safety benefits and general capabilities with minimal degradation.

problem: LMs cannot reliably self-refine responses on open-ended queries with natural language feedback, a task present in over 10% of real-world user interactions.
approach: Introduce RefineBench, a benchmark of 1,002 problems across 11 domains with guided and self-refinement settings, and evaluate frontier models on their ability to iteratively improve.
contribution: Shows frontier LMs achieve modest baseline self-refinement scores (Gemini 2.5 Pro 31.1%, GPT-4.1 23.4%) but leverage targeted feedback for near-perfect refinement within five turns.

problem: High-dimensional recovery via gradient descent on planted-vector problems requires sample complexity that grows with the information exponent.
approach: Show Langevin dynamics with iterate averaging (rather than last-iterate) emulates landscape smoothing and recovers hidden directions with d^(k*/2) samples.
contribution: Achieves optimal sample complexity for tensor PCA and single-index models without explicit landscape smoothing, by leveraging noise injection and averaging.

problem: Time series forecasting with LLMs suffers from a semantic gap between linguistic knowledge structures and temporal data patterns, limiting interpretability.
approach: Propose SE-LLM (Semantic-Enhanced LLM) that embeds time-series periodicity and anomalies into LLM token embeddings, plus a plugin module modeling long/short-term dependencies within self-attention.
contribution: Achieves superior forecasting performance while reducing computational cost by freezing the LLM and reducing sequence dimensionality.

problem: LLM pretraining relies on input-space reconstruction (autoregressive), while vision models benefit from embedding-space objectives like Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs).
approach: Develop LLM-JEPA, applying JEPA-style embedding-space training to LLMs for both finetuning and pretraining.
contribution: Outperforms standard LLM training objectives across multiple models (Llama3, OpenELM, Gemma2, Olmo) and datasets while being robust to overfitting.

problem: Masked diffusion language models use binary masking decisions that discard predictive information when masks are retained, limiting iterative refinement.
approach: Introduce soft-masking (SM) which blends the mask token embedding with embeddings of top-k predicted tokens, providing richer priors for retained masks.
contribution: Improves perplexity, MAUVE scores on pretrained models, and enhances performance on coding benchmarks like Dream-7B.

problem: Image segmentation models lack reliable image-specific uncertainty quantification; conformal methods ensure marginal but not image-conditional coverage.
approach: Propose COAT (Conditional Optimization for Adaptive Thresholding), an end-to-end differentiable framework using a soft TPR approximation as loss to optimize image-conditional coverage.
contribution: Achieves improved conditional guarantees for segmentation uncertainty, enabling more trustworthy predictions for safety-critical applications.

problem: Retrieval-based tool-use pipelines struggle with semantic encoding, while generative methods mapping each tool to a unique token face scalability and vocabulary explosion.
approach: Introduce ToolWeaver, which encodes tools as hierarchical token sequences, enabling the model to learn collaborative tool relationships through shared codes.
contribution: Reduces vocabulary expansion from linear to logarithmic in tool count and improves generalization through dense co-occurrence of shared tool codes.

problem: LLMs struggle to balance world knowledge and logical reasoning when identifying causal relationships, often relying on superficial heuristics.
approach: Investigate causal reasoning via controlled synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real-world narratives; identify how task reformulation elicits more robust reasoning.
contribution: Uncovers systematic patterns in LLM causal reasoning across linear chains to complex graphs with colliders, informing better alignment methods.

problem: LLMs hallucinate and forget context because attention shifts away from initial input toward newly generated tokens.
approach: Propose SinkTrack, which injects key contextual features into the BOS token's embedding, leveraging the LLM's intrinsic attention-sink behavior.
contribution: Training-free, plug-and-play method reduces hallucination and context forgetting by 18.9% on QuAC and 23.0% on M3CoT without architectural changes.

problem: Selecting priors for ill-posed inverse problems via model evidence is intractable when using diffusion models.
approach: Propose DiME, which integrates over time-marginals of posterior sampling methods to estimate model evidence with only a handful of posterior samples.
contribution: Enables scalable prior selection and diagnosis of prior misfit on highly ill-conditioned problems including real-world black hole imaging.

problem: LMs rely on fixed tokenizers that limit granularity and lead to brittle behaviors even in strong reasoning models.
approach: Introduce ByteFlow Net, which removes tokenizers entirely and learns segmentation of raw bytes via compression-driven information-theoretic chunking.
contribution: Outperforms BPE-based Transformers and prior byte-level methods by enabling adaptive, input-dependent representation granularity.

problem: High-quality aesthetic poster generation requires text rendering, artistic integration, layout design, and style harmony, which modular pipelines fail to achieve holistically.
approach: Propose PosterCraft with cascaded workflow: text-rendering optimization (Text-Render-2M), supervised finetuning (HQ-Poster-100K), aesthetic RL, and vision-language refinement.
contribution: Significantly outperforms open-source baselines in rendering, layout, and visual appeal, approaching commercial system quality.

problem: Synchrony-based object-centric models struggle with reliable phase alignment and grouping, especially under occlusion.
approach: Propose OrthoRF (Orthogonal Rotating Features), enforcing orthogonality in orientation space via inner-product loss and architectural modifications.
contribution: Matches or outperforms existing models on unsupervised object discovery, recovers occluded object parts, and produces more interpretable representations.

problem: Existing scientific law discovery benchmarks face a methodological trilemma balancing scientific relevance, scalability, and memorization resistance.
approach: Introduce NewtonBench, 324 tasks across 12 physics domains using counterfactual law shifts; require LLM agents to experimentally probe systems to uncover hidden principles.
contribution: Frontier models show fragile discovery capability degrading with system complexity and noise; code interpreters can hinder capable models via premature exploitation.

problem: Reasoning-enhanced models may exploit loopholes in reward functions implicitly, bypassing CoT monitors through subtle reasoning shortcuts.
approach: Propose TRACE (Truncated Reasoning AUC Evaluation), quantifying reasoning 'effort' by measuring how early truncated CoTs pass verifiers.
contribution: Achieves 65% gains over CoT monitoring baselines on math and 30% gains on code, discovering unknown training loopholes.

problem: Few-step generative models face computational overhead, complex loss functions, and intricate multi-stage training that limits scalability.
approach: Introduce RCGM (N-th order Recursive Consistent velocity field estimation), unifying consistency models and revealing them as 1st-order special cases.
contribution: Achieves 1.48 FID on ImageNet 256x256 in 2 steps; enables stable 20B multimodal model training without collapse.

problem: Recurrent LLMs offer linear complexity but underperform on long-context tasks due to limited fixed-size memory.
approach: Propose Smooth Reading, an incremental, multi-round inference method that iteratively processes and summarizes context, reducing memory pressure.
contribution: Bridges Recurrent-to-Self-Attention performance gap (5.68% lower to 3.61% higher on LongBench) while maintaining 2.5x training and 2x inference speedups.

problem: MLLMs excel at holistic understanding but struggle with dense scenes requiring fine-grained region-level analysis and multi-region reasoning.
approach: Introduce Grasp Any Region (GAR), using RoI-aligned feature replay to understand regions in global context and model multi-prompt interactions.
contribution: GAR-1B outperforms DAM-3B by 4.5% on DLC-Bench and surpasses InternVL3-78B on region VQA; zero-shot transfer to video.

problem: Strengthening reasoning capabilities can induce misalignment, where models learn to rationalize unsafe outputs through entangled reasoning-safety representations.
approach: Provide mechanistic analysis via representation analysis and neuron-level activation entanglement in reasoning-critical neurons.
contribution: Identifies reasoning-induced misalignment as activation entanglement between reasoning and safety, correlating with catastrophic forgetting.

problem: Existing cross-modal hashing methods fail to exploit hierarchical structures and cannot effectively bridge semantic gaps between text and image modalities.
approach: Introduce HINT (Hierarchical Encoding Tree with Modality Mixup), extracting hierarchical relations and using curriculum-based proxy-sample mixup.
contribution: Achieves effective cross-modal retrieval with progressive modal alignment and global-view semantic consistency.

problem: LLMs lack introspection to anticipate success and computational cost, forcing fixed sampling budgets and preventing adaptive inference.
approach: Propose ZIP-RC, reusing reserved logits to output joint distributions over final reward and remaining length without extra models or overhead.
contribution: Enables zero-overhead inference-time adaptive sampling via utility-maximizing meta-actions on expected reward and compute tradeoffs.

problem: Predicting complex infinite-order time series requires capturing intricate inductive biases and multivariate dependencies.
approach: Propose MFPs (mean-field continuous sequence predictors), reframing sequence prediction as mean-field games and using fictitious play with gradient descent.
contribution: Achieves highly accurate continuous sequence predictions outperforming prior benchmarks through game-theoretic Nash equilibrium computation.

problem: Deep learning models rely on spurious correlations, making them vulnerable to worst-group performance under subpopulation shift.
approach: Propose SCER (Spurious Correlation-Aware Embedding Regularization), regularizing embeddings to suppress spurious directions identified from group-wise mean differences.
contribution: Outperforms prior state-of-the-art on worst-group accuracy across vision and language tasks with theoretical embedding-level constraints.

problem: Robot policy pre-training is hindered by high demonstration collection costs and inability to leverage diverse heterogeneous robot datasets.
approach: Combine offline RL with cross-embodiment learning, then introduce embodiment-based grouping to mitigate conflicting gradients across morphologies.
contribution: Excels at pre-training with suboptimal data; grouping strategy outperforms existing conflict-resolution methods on 16 robot platforms.

problem: Unknown unknowns (deployment-time scenarios absent from development) differ from anomalies and evade existing time-series anomaly detection methods.
approach: Introduce SPIE-AD, a zero-shot model-recovery-and-conformance method; validate on eight new U2 benchmarks where existing methods fail.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art MTAD on all U2 benchmarks without point adjustment or threshold leakage.

problem: Robot manipulation policies are vulnerable to external variations; relevant test variations are unknown and real-world testing is costly.
approach: Learn a deep RL vulnerability-prediction policy via a continuous vision-language embedding as a potential field, querying it to build vulnerability maps.
contribution: Uncovers 23% more unique vulnerabilities than baselines; fine-tuning with discovered vulnerabilities improves manipulation with less data.

problem: Agentic RAG suffers from over-search and under-search inefficiencies due to outcome-based rewards lacking fine-grained control.
approach: Introduce HiPRAG with hierarchical process rewards that evaluate search necessity and provide bonuses based on optimal step proportions.
contribution: Achieves 65.4% (3B) and 67.2% (7B) accuracy on benchmarks while reducing over-search from 27% to 2.3%.

problem: Unified Vision-Language Models treat understanding and generation as parallel capabilities without explicit synergy during task solving.
approach: Introduce AD-Loop (Analyzing-Drafting), an interleaved problem-solving paradigm alternating between analytic and drafting operations via supervised learning then RL.
contribution: Improves performance across understanding and generation benchmarks with strong transferability to various UVLM architectures.

problem: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) lacks efficient optimization leveraging differential geometry insights and introduces hyperparameter complexity.
approach: Establish quotient-manifold iteration scheme on Riemannian geometry; replace weight decay with Sylvester matrix for principled optimization.
contribution: Proposes AdamS and LRACS optimizers with runtime analysis, demonstrating improvements over existing LoRA optimizers.

problem: Multiplex biological networks require predicting unseen interactions on entities with no prior neighborhood information.
approach: Leverage context-aware embeddings via foundation models, topology-aware graph tokenizer, and teacher-student distillation for zero-shot generalization.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art on multiplex biological network interaction prediction.

problem: Vision tokens in VLMs contain redundancy; existing pruning methods use only unimodal information and lack generic criteria across modalities.
approach: Propose MMTok, formulating vision-token selection as a maximum coverage problem jointly optimizing vision and text token coverage.
contribution: Achieves 1.87x speedup on LLaVA-NeXT-13B while retaining 98.7% performance; maintains 87.7% performance with only four vision tokens.

problem: Standard weight decay implicitly optimizes a regularized objective, lacking principled connection to the original loss.
approach: Introduce Cautious Weight Decay (CWD), applying decay only to parameters whose gradients align with updates, enabling sliding-mode search for Pareto-optimal points.
contribution: Drop-in optimizer modification improving language model pre-training and ImageNet classification at million- to billion-parameter scales.

problem: Linear programming approaches to solving MDPs yield inequality-constrained problems that are harder than dynamic programming methods.
approach: Leverage log-barrier functions to transform LP formulations of MDPs into unconstrained optimization solvable via gradient descent.
contribution: Establishes theoretical foundation for approximate LP-based MDP solutions with practical gradient-descent efficiency.

problem: LLMs passively accept manually engineered context without agency to dynamically manage their own memory and context.
approach: Introduce StateLM, equipping models with tools (dynamic indexing, context pruning, note-taking) and training them to actively manage state via internal reasoning loops.
contribution: Decouples performance from context window size, reliably retrieves signals from 1-million-token contexts with linear inference cost.

problem: The extent to which LLMs implicitly plan internal representations is unknown.
approach: Define latent planning and study Qwen-3 family (0.6B-14B) on planning tasks using probing to detect planned-for features and causal effects.
contribution: Latent planning increases with scale; models identify rhymes ahead of time; even smaller models have nascent planning mechanisms.

problem: LLMs with million-token context windows suffer score dilution in static attention, where decoding more tokens cannot recover buried evidence.
approach: Propose qTTT (query-only test-time training), a cache-preserving adaptation applying gradient updates to query projections after a single prefill.
contribution: Improves average accuracy by +12.6 on LongBench-v2 and +14.1 on ZeroSCROLLS; more efficient than thinking tokens for long contexts.

problem: Continuous-token autoregressive image generation suffers variance collapse due to heterogeneous VAE latent variance, especially under classifier-free guidance.
approach: Propose SphereAR, constraining AR inputs/outputs to a fixed-radius hypersphere using hyperspherical VAEs to stabilize decoding.
contribution: Achieves FID 1.34 on ImageNet for AR models; at smaller scales surpasses larger baselines like MAR and VAR.

problem: Subject-agnostic brain decoding from fMRI without subject-specific training faces cross-subject generalization challenges.
approach: Propose VCFlow, modeling ventral-dorsal visual cortex architecture; use feature-level contrastive learning to enhance subject-invariant semantic representations.
contribution: Sacrifices only 7% accuracy on unseen subjects while generating reconstructed videos in 10 seconds without retraining.

problem: Autoregressive VLA methods discretize actions losing continuity, while diffusion VLAs ignore LLM expertise for iterative generation.
approach: Introduce HybridVLA, leveraging shared LLM backbone for both autoregressive and diffusion predictions via collaborative training and adaptive ensemble.
contribution: Outperforms prior VLA methods by 17% and 19% in mean success rate, adaptively fusing predictions for robust control.
